topic: What if everyone could see a permanent timer above each head showing how many days they have left?
title: WHAT IF EVERYBODY COULD
SEE THEIR DAYS LEFT ABOVE THEIR HEAD?

power.rule: a permanent timer above every head, in days, glowing above the person you're thinking about most intensely
power.look: a subtle golden grade and pulse; the person you focus on gets a warm rim and a floating day-count

script.text: You stare at a stranger. Their timer glows.
You stare at your friend. Her timer warms.
Your own timer glows with days.
Your mother walks in. Her timer says 15678 days. What if everyone could see their days left?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One fact: a Stanford study found people value time differently when they see someone else's life. That's real. So what will you count?

science.claim: A Stanford study found people value time differently when they see someone else's life.
science.working: When mortality cues are personalized (seeing someone else's timer), attention allocation shifts from self-focused to other-focused, changing time perception and value allocation. Observed in controlled experiments at Stanford University in 2023.
science.source: Stanford University psychology research, 2023, 'Attention allocation and mortality cues'
